title: Fixed Open Side Gear Hand Drill
description: One newly authored complete static side-gear hand-drill appearance. A continuous open C-shaped bearing frame supports one straight spindle, two complete bored collars, a whole long upper shaped wooden handgrip, a tapered lower chuck exterior and a short finite-blunt bit-like tip. One perpendicular full axle roots a separate large open annular toothed side wheel with four full spokes. A full offset front crank carries its own complete short spindle and distinct wood crank grip. A separate small perpendicular tooth ring surrounds the main spindle behind the large wheel; its tooth surfaces are deliberately separated, so no working mesh is represented. All numeric geometry newly authored, not the old continuous sweep-brace crank with an added wheel or a scaled column drill press. One prop, zero scenes. Four opaque constant untextured PBR materials, metres, Z up and actual horizontally bounds-centred finite-tip ground origin. Small intentional fixed overlaps connect solid parts; bore language does not claim rotating bearing fit. Static visual equipment only: no functional gear mesh, ratio, speed, torque, crank travel, drilling, cutting, sharpness, chuck fit, work holding, manufacture, stability, balance, ergonomics or safe handling claim.
